deep.reconstruction:
The page has two blocks. Both deal with algebraic curves defined by relations among square roots of forms in homogeneous coordinates (x:y:z). This matches the surrounding 'AbelTheta' material: the previous page carries Fano-plane-like 7-index bookkeeping, typical of genus-3 / bitangent combinatorics.

BLOCK 1 (rationalising a square-root curve equation).
(1) Riemann writes a curve equation
  d z sqrt((x+y+z)^2 + m x y) + sqrt((x-alpha z)(x-beta z)(y-gamma z)(y-delta z)) = xy + z(ax+by+cz).
  He abbreviates the linear form q := ax+by+cz, so the right side is xy + zq.
  He then generalises the quadric under the first root to the normal form xy + p^2, with p a linear form. This is a ternary quadric written as xy + p^2.
(2) Squaring. Write A = d z sqrt(xy+p^2), B = sqrt(L1 L2 L3 L4), C = xy + zq. From A + B = C he forms A^2 + B^2 - C^2 = -2AB, i.e.
  d^2 z^2 (xy+p^2) + (x-alpha z)(x-beta z)(y-gamma z)(y-delta z) - (xy+zq)^2 = (+/-) 2 d z sqrt(xy+p^2) sqrt(quartic).
  He writes only 'sqrt sqrt' with '2 d z' underneath; the sign is absorbed in the branch.
(3) He groups the quartic into two binary quadratics:
  (x-alpha z)(x-beta z) = x^2 + 2a x z + b z^2,
  (y-gamma z)(y-delta z) = y^2 + 2a' y z + b' z^2.
  Here 2a = -(alpha+beta), b = alpha*beta, and similarly for a', b'. Note the letters a, b are reused; they clash with q = ax+by+cz.
  Expansion of the product: x^2y^2 + z[y^2(2ax+bz) + x^2(2a'y+b'z)] + z^2(2ax+bz)(2a'y+b'z). On the page the factor z on the middle terms is omitted in the intermediate line.
(4) The x^2 y^2 terms cancel against (xy+zq)^2 = x^2y^2 + 2xyzq + z^2q^2. Dividing by z gives the cubic form
  K = d^2 z (xy+p^2) + y^2(2ax+bz) + x^2(2a'y+b'z) + z(2ax+bz)(2a'y+b'z) - 2xyq - zq^2.
  This equals (+/-) 2 d sqrt((x^2+2axz+bz^2)(y^2+2a'yz+b'z^2)(xy+p^2)).
  So the original curve becomes 'cubic = 2d * sqrt(product of three conics)', i.e. K^2 = 4 d^2 Q1 Q2 Q3.
  He labels this cubic 'q - v = q''. The precise meaning of v here is not recoverable with certainty (my reading).

BLOCK 2 (three-term square-root relations among products of linear forms).
The letters u, v, p, q, p', q', t now denote forms (presumably linear), and alpha, beta are constants.
(5) He first writes q'·sqrt(u p') = alpha sqrt(p'q'uq) - beta sqrt(p'q'pv), with q' = q - v. Dividing by sqrt(q') gives
  sqrt(q' u p') = alpha sqrt(p' u q) - beta sqrt(p' p v).
  (The image shows sqrt(up); the factor should be sqrt(up') for consistency.)
(6) He sets
  f^2 = u v p q t,
  phi^2 = u v p' q' t,
  psi^2 = p q p' q' t.
  Then (f - alpha phi)(f + alpha phi) = f^2 - alpha^2 phi^2 = u v (pq - alpha^2 p'q') t.
(7) He imposes the condition u(pq - alpha^2 p'q') + v t = 2 sqrt(uvpqt) = 2f.
  Since (sqrt(upq) - sqrt(vt))^2 = upq + vt - 2f, the condition is equivalent to
  sqrt(upq) - sqrt(vt) = alpha sqrt(p'q'u).
  (The '+' on the page is struck; the sign is minus.)
  Likewise p(uv - beta^2 p'q') + q t = 2f is equivalent to sqrt(puv) - sqrt(qt) = beta sqrt(p'q'p).
(8) The condition in (7) and the product in (6) give a split factorisation:
  f + alpha phi = u(pq - alpha^2 p'q'),  f - alpha phi = v t.
  Their sum is 2f, their product is f^2 - alpha^2 phi^2.
  In the same way:
  f + beta psi = p(uv - beta^2 p'q'),  f - beta psi = q t.
(9) Subtracting the two minus-equations:
  beta psi - alpha phi = (f - alpha phi) - (f - beta psi) = v t - q t = (v - q) t.
  He sets v - q = q' (earlier he wrote q - v = q'; the sign convention is flipped). This gives
  beta sqrt(pqp'q't) - alpha sqrt(uvp'q't) = q' t, i.e. beta sqrt(pq p') - alpha sqrt(uv p') = sqrt(q' t) after dividing by sqrt(p'q't)/sqrt(q') (my step).
  So two three-term root relations of 'Riemann/Hesse type' combine into a third. This is the kind of manipulation used to pass between representations sqrt(A) + sqrt(B) + sqrt(C) = 0 of a plane quartic, or between bitangent-product relations.
errors: Intermediate expansion line 'x^2y^2 + y^2(2ax+bz) + x^2(2a'y+b'z)' omits the factor z on the last two terms. The next full line is correct after division by z, so this is a harmless slip in a scratch line.
Notational clash: a, b first denote coefficients in q = ax+by+cz, then are reused for the coefficients of x^2+2axz+bz^2.
Sign of q' is inconsistent: 'q - v = q'' in the middle of the page, but 'v - q = q'' at the bottom (and beta psi - alpha phi = (v-q)t).
In '(q-v) sqrt(up) = alpha sqrt(p'q'uq) - beta sqrt(p'q'pv)', consistency with the next line sqrt(q'up') = ... requires sqrt(up'), not sqrt(up). This is either a slip or a lost prime.
The squaring step A^2+B^2-C^2 = -2AB carries a minus sign, which is suppressed (absorbed into the choice of branch). This is not an error.

results.what: Rationalising a plane curve given by d z sqrt(xy+p^2) + sqrt(product of four lines) = conic into the form (cubic)^2 = 4 d^2 * (product of three conics)
results.modern_name: elimination of radicals / representation of a plane curve by a square-root equation (contact curves)
results.usually_credited_to: standard algebraic technique (Plücker, Hesse, Cayley era)

results.what: Three-term square-root relations sqrt(upq) - sqrt(vt) = alpha sqrt(up'q'), equivalent to f +/- alpha phi factorising as u(pq - alpha^2 p'q') and vt; combining two such relations gives beta psi - alpha phi = (v-q)t
results.modern_name: relations among bitangents / contact conics; sqrt(x xi) + sqrt(y eta) + sqrt(z zeta) = 0 representations of the plane quartic (Riemann–Aronhold–Hesse)
results.usually_credited_to: Hesse (1855), Steiner, Aronhold (1864); Riemann 1865 lectures on p=3 (published via H. Weber 1876)

deep.surprise_reason: These are algebraic scratch manipulations: squaring out radical relations and factoring f^2 - alpha^2 phi^2. They fit Riemann's known genus-3 / bitangent work (Weber 1876) and the Fano-plane bookkeeping on the previous page. Nothing beyond known material is established on this page.

transcription_corrections: Line 'sqrt(upq) [-+-] sqrt(vt) = alpha sqrt(p'q'u)': the '+' is struck and the relation is with a minus sign: sqrt(upq) - sqrt(vt) = alpha sqrt(p'q'u).

In 'f+alpha phi = [-u-](...)', 'f-alpha phi = [-v-]t', 'f+beta psi = [-p-](...)', 'f-beta psi = [-q-]t' the leading letters are heavily inked or overwritten, not deleted. They should be read as u, v, p, q, as the algebra requires.
'(q-v)sqrt(up)' should probably read '(q-v)sqrt(up')' (q' sqrt(up') = ...), to be consistent with the following line.
The crossed-out phrase at the end of the first line is '+sqrt((x+y+z)^2+mxy)'. The crossed line on the left is 'd^2 z^2 (x+y+z)^2'.
The '2 d z' under the radicals in the squared equation is the coefficient of the product sqrt()sqrt() on the right-hand side.
The intermediate line 'x^2y^2 + y^2(2ax+bz) + x^2(2a'y+b'z)' is as written; the z factors are missing in the original, not a transcription error.
